summary: Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
Richard B. Martin is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He served at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and trained under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center, serving as abbot (1971–1984), and later founded Dharma Sangha.
Richard Barron works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees, including a Litt.D, at the University of Cambridge. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, and Cambridge, serving as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who attended Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal Staff Corps and Indian Army, owned the Indian Antiquary (~1884–1931), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.
Richard D. Mann works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at McMaster University (attested 2003) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Richard D. McBride II is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UCLA under mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University.

Richard Delbrueck (1875–1957) was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1900–1909), the University of Jena (~1911–1928), and the University of Giessen (~1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 2004. As attested in 2013, he served as Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University.

Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who studied at Kiel University. He worked at the Kiel University Library, Prussian State Library, and Göttingen State and University Library, and was an honorary professor at the University of Göttingen from 1923.

Richard Foltz is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, religious, and historical studies who earned degrees from the University of Utah and Harvard University. He taught at several institutions before becoming Founding Director at Concordia University (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche (b. 1851) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus. He held a post as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

Richard Gombrich is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his BA and DPhil at Oxford, studying under Walpola Rahula, Gananath Obeyesekere, and Robert Charles Zaehner. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1965–2004).

Richard Hartshorne (1899–1992) studied at Princeton University and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).

Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena, training under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. He served as Lektor at the University of Jena and joined the Saxon Academy of Sciences.

Richard Henebry (1863–1916) was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's College, Maynooth, and the universities of Greifswald and Freiburg. He studied under Heinrich Zimmer between ~1895 and ~1898.

Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Alberta and the University of London. After teaching at the University of Toronto, he became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1987). In ~1994, he became Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College.

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University and Harvard University. He held academic positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as a psychology professor there from 2001 to 2017.
